issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Farm constructor with no arguments (the instructions explicitly say to initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments and the provided Main uses new Farm()), but the solution implements only a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor and provides no no-arg constructor. This constructor-parameter mismatch means the straightforward no-arg usage shown in the template/Main (and required by the specification) would not compile against the solution implementation and will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Optionally keep the Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor as an overload. This aligns the solution with the problem statement and the usage in Main.
